mainTopicBrief: 本单元围绕前沿科技展开，涵盖人工智能的机遇与风险（Reading）、虚拟现实的应用前景（Extended reading）和时间胶囊·写给未来（Integrated skills）三个子话题——AI 与未来科技是高考应用文'科技节/建议信'类的热门场景，更是近年雅思科技类议论文的第一高频命题。

subTopics.title: AI的机遇与风险
subTopics.titleEn: The Promise and Peril of AI
subTopics.desc: 课文核心：AI is already being applied in many fields: finance, health care, machine translation and art, to name but a few——但有识之士 urge us to think about the dangers posed by the advances in AI。

prompts.task: 你校科技节以 "AI in Our Lives" 为主题征集英文短文。请你投稿，内容包括：1. AI 在生活中的应用；2. 人们的担忧；3. 你的看法。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
When my grandfather asks his smart speaker to play Beijing opera, he is chatting with artificial intelligence without knowing it. Given the rate at which AI is being developed, such scenes are becoming part of daily life.

Nowadays, AI is already being applied in many fields: finance, health care, machine translation and art, to name but a few. With the capacity to analyse massive amounts of data, it helps doctors find diseases earlier and translators work faster. Some scientists, however, urge us to think about the dangers posed by the advances in AI, warning that we might fall victim to the very tools we create. Apparently, such warnings demand our attention.

In my view, AI is neither an angel nor a devil. Whether it serves us or threatens us boils down to how wisely we humans use it.
vocabHints: the capacity to analyse massive amounts of data
the dangers posed by the advances in AI

prompts.task: Some people believe that developments in artificial intelligence will cause many people to lose their jobs, while others think AI will create more opportunities than it destroys. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Predictions about artificial intelligence swing between nightmare and utopia: mass unemployment on one side, unprecedented opportunity on the other. Examining both claims, I conclude that AI will transform work far more than it destroys it — but the transition will punish societies that fail to prepare for it.

The fear of job losses is grounded in visible fact. Machine systems already draft documents, answer customer calls, inspect products and drive vehicles in trials, and they work continuously without wages. Unlike earlier waves of automation, AI reaches into white-collar territory — accounting, translation, even routine medical analysis — so workers who believed education protected them now feel exposed. When change arrives faster than retraining, entire communities can be stranded, as former industrial regions still testify.

Optimists answer with history and arithmetic. Every major technology, from the tractor to the internet, ended some occupations while creating others that earlier generations could not imagine; today millions work in fields that did not exist twenty years ago. AI itself demands data specialists, safety auditors and engineers, and by cutting costs it expands demand elsewhere in the economy. Crucially, machines complement rather than duplicate human strengths: empathy, ethical judgement and creative leadership continue to resist automation.

My own view is that the outcome depends less on the technology than on policy. Governments that invest in lifelong retraining, portable benefits and strong safety nets can convert disruption into productivity; those that leave workers alone with the shock invite inequality and anger. AI, in short, will not decide our employment future — the way we govern it will.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点论据扎实(失业方:白领岗位失守/再培训跟不上;机会方:历史规律/新职业/成本下降扩需求)，立场'转型大于毁灭+取决于政策'层次分明，结论把裁决权从技术移交给治理。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):The fear / Optimists answer / My own view 推进干净;'nightmare vs utopia'开题张力贯穿全文;分号对仗(Governments that invest...; those that leave...)完成政策对比。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):reaches into white-collar territory / stranded / portable benefits / convert disruption into productivity / leave workers alone with the shock 等表达兼具专业性与画面感。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):Examining分词开题、Unlike介词对比、as former industrial regions still testify插入例证、from...to...列举、强调倒装收尾(the way we govern it will)，句式丰富准确。
vsGaokao: 体裁:高考写科技节征文(现象+担忧+态度);雅思写就业影响双边议论文。
论据来源:高考短文织入课文'to name but a few / fall victim to'词块并可用生活化开头;雅思用劳动经济学普适论据(自动化历史、再培训政策)。
语域:征文允许祖父与智能音箱的生活场景;雅思例证以类别呈现(accounting, translation, routine medical analysis)。

subTopics.title: 预见未来的科技
subTopics.desc: 语法板块核心词块：It can be predicted that、sth is predicted to do、decrease by、on the increase——想象无人机送货的那一天，也是在练习'预测'这一实用表达。

prompts.task: 你校科技社团举办 "Tech in 2035" 主题征文。请你写一篇短文，预测一项科技将如何改变未来生活，内容包括：1. 你预测的科技；2. 它带来的改变；3. 你的看法。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
What will daily life look like in 2035? Here is my prediction.

It can be predicted that before long many people will be using drones to deliver daily supplies like food and medicine. Such a change is predicted to save a great deal of time and greatly decrease road traffic; the number of delivery vans on our streets could decrease by a third. Meanwhile, the demand for fast, green transport is clearly on the increase.

Of course, no technology is perfect, and questions of safety and privacy will need careful answers. Still, I believe the future is something we invent, not simply wait for. If we guide new tools wisely, tomorrow can be both faster and kinder.
vocabHints: is predicted to save a great deal of time

prompts.task: Some people are optimistic that scientific and technological progress will solve most of the world's problems, while others are more pessimistic. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Each new breakthrough revives an old debate: will science and technology eventually solve humanity's problems, or merely create new ones? Optimists trust progress to save us; pessimists fear it will do as much harm as good. Having weighed both, I believe technology is a powerful tool whose value depends entirely on how wisely people choose to use it.

The optimistic case is supported by history. Science has doubled human lifespans, defeated diseases that once wiped out millions, and multiplied food production far beyond what earlier generations thought possible. It can be predicted that further advances in medicine, clean energy and artificial intelligence will ease suffering on a similar scale, and past pessimists who declared problems unsolvable have often been proved wrong.

Yet the pessimists are not merely gloomy. The same science that cures also builds weapons capable of ending civilisation; industrial progress has warmed the planet dangerously; and each solution seems to breed fresh difficulties, from digital addiction to the threat of mass unemployment. Technology, crucially, has no conscience of its own — it amplifies whatever intentions guide it, for good or ill.

This is why I place my faith not in technology alone but in the wisdom directing it. The atom can light a city or destroy one; the difference lies entirely in human choice. Progress supplies ever more powerful tools, but whether they heal or harm depends on the values, laws and cooperation of the people who wield them.

In conclusion, science and technology can solve enormous problems, yet they guarantee nothing on their own. Our future rests less on what we can build than on how responsibly we decide to build it.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点均展开(乐观:寿命/抗疫/粮食;悲观:武器/气候/新问题)，立场'技术是工具、取决于智慧'贯穿，结论把裁决权交给'如何负责任地建造'。
Coherence & Cohesion(连贯衔接):optimistic case / Yet the pessimists / This is why / In conclusion 推进清晰;'no conscience of its own'与'atom lights or destroys'意象点睛;'It can be predicted that'织入单元词块。
Lexical Resource(词汇资源):revives an old debate / breed fresh difficulties / amplifies whatever intentions guide it / heal or harm 表达精准有力。
Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):whose定语从句、that复指、not...but平行、less on...than on收尾比较，句式多样。

论据来源:高考短文织入课件'it can be predicted that / is predicted to / decrease by / on the increase'词块;雅思用科技史的普适论据。
语域:征文有设问与展望(What will life look like?);雅思客观权衡，'工具无良知'显思辨。

subTopics.title: 时间胶囊·写给未来
subTopics.desc: 综合技能板块核心：The time capsule, buried 50 feet below the ground, was designed to be opened in the year 6939——把 contemporary 生活的切片寄给未来。

prompts.task: 你校英语社团开展'时间胶囊'活动：写一封信封存于校园，二十年后由未来的学弟学妹开启。请你用英文写这封信，内容包括：1. 介绍当下的校园生活；2. 你对未来读者的祝愿。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear students of 2046,

By the time you read this letter, it will have slept in a time capsule buried in the corner of our school garden for twenty years. Like the famous capsule designed to be opened in the year 6939, ours carries messages from one age to another.

Let me tell you about our contemporary school life. We still write essays by hand, though AI is already being applied in many fields. We worry about exams, play basketball after class, and dream about the future — perhaps the very world you are living in now.

Whatever has changed, I believe some things remain: friendship, curiosity and hard work. Take good care of them for us.

Yours from 2026,
Li Hua
vocabHints: carry messages from one age to another

prompts.task: Some people spend a lot of time planning for the future, while others believe it is more important to focus on the present. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Some people devote their energy to mapping out the years ahead, while others insist that life happens only in the present moment. Both instincts contain wisdom, and in my view a fulfilled life depends on keeping them in deliberate balance, with planning serving the present rather than replacing it.

The argument for looking forward is intensely practical. Education, savings, health and careers all reward those who sacrifice early for later gain; the student who prepares months before an examination outperforms the one who trusts inspiration on the day. Planning also cushions misfortune: insurance, emergency funds and preventive check-ups exist precisely because the future is uncertain. At the level of whole societies, refusing to think ahead — about climate, pensions or infrastructure — simply transfers today's comfort into tomorrow's crisis.

Champions of the present reply that tomorrow is a promise no one can enforce. People who postpone happiness until retirement often find that health or circumstances have changed beyond recognition, and chronic worry about what may come poisons what already is. Psychology supports them: attention to the present moment — time with family, absorption in meaningful work, gratitude for small pleasures — correlates strongly with wellbeing, while excessive future-focus feeds anxiety.

The wisest arrangement, I would argue, treats planning as a servant of living. We should set directions, prepare for reasonable risks, and then return our attention to the day itself, revisiting the map occasionally instead of staring at it. To plan without living is to miss one's own life; to live without planning is to gamble it. Neither mistake deserves imitation.

bandFeatures: Task Response(任务回应):双观点各有完整主体段(规划方:教育储蓄保险+社会层面;当下方:延迟幸福的代价+心理学证据)，立场'规划服务于当下'在开头结尾一致，并给出可操作的平衡法(revisiting the map occasionally)。

Grammatical Range & Accuracy(语法多样性):with复合结构、precisely because强调因果、破折号插入列举、对仗警句(To plan without living...; to live without planning...)，句式张弛有度。

语域:书信有想象与温情(it will have slept in a time capsule);雅思理性思辨，抒情仅存于隐喻。

subTopics.title: VR的应用与前景
subTopics.desc: 拓展阅读核心：VR 是 immersive technology，拥有 a host of educational applications——能 engage students' interest and enhance learning efficiency，尽管 the initial cost 仍是障碍。

prompts.task: 请你用英文给校长写一封建议信，建议学校引进虚拟现实（VR）技术辅助教学，内容包括：1. 写信目的；2. VR 教学的好处；3. 可行的做法。注意：词数100左右。
prompts.reference:
Dear Mr Headmaster,

I am Li Hua, a Senior 2 student. I am writing to suggest introducing virtual reality technology into our classes.

VR is an immersive technology with a host of educational applications. In a geography class, for example, students could "stand" on a glacier instead of staring at flat pictures; in chemistry, dangerous experiments could be practised safely. Such experiences engage students' interest and enhance learning efficiency in a way ordinary slides can hardly match.

Admittedly, the initial cost may discourage us in the beginning, but that could be fixed over time — the school might start with one shared VR classroom and open it to different subjects in turn.

Thank you for considering my suggestion. I would be glad to help organise a trial lesson.

Yours sincerely,
Li Hua

prompts.task: Some people believe that immersive technologies such as virtual reality will make traditional classrooms unnecessary in the future. To what extent do you agree or disagree? (Write at least 250 words.)
prompts.reference:
Some futurists announce that immersive technologies such as virtual reality will soon make the traditional classroom unnecessary: why gather thirty children in one room when any lesson can be experienced through a headset? I disagree with this prediction in its strong form, although I expect virtual tools to reshape schooling profoundly.

The attractions of virtual learning are genuine. A headset can transport students inside a volcano, an ancient city or a human cell, turning abstractions into experience that textbooks cannot match. Lessons can be replayed at each learner's own pace, rural schools can enter laboratories they could never afford to build, and dangerous procedures — chemical reactions, emergency medicine — can be practised without risk. Used well, such immersion deepens both interest and memory.

Yet education is far more than the delivery of vivid content. Classrooms teach children to wait their turn, argue respectfully, cooperate with people they did not choose, and accept guidance from adults — social capacities no simulation reproduces, because the other minds in the room must be real. Teachers do more than transmit information: they notice confusion on a face, adjust the lesson in the moment and provide the encouragement on which motivation depends. Long hours inside headsets also raise health concerns, from eyesight to isolation, that no parent can dismiss.

For these reasons I believe the future is blended rather than purely virtual. Schools will remain the social heart of education, while VR serves as a powerful instrument within them — an extraordinary window, but not a substitute for the human room around it. Technology should enrich the classroom, not abolish it.
